collection.description: Someone tells the old family crab story wrong at a gathering: correct them, or let the new version live.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Every family gathering, someone tells the story about the time an old relative was chased all the way up the beach by a crab "the size of a basket." Everyone knows it by heart. Tonight (friend) tells it, and gets it wrong: in (friend.his/her) version it was a cooking pot, not a basket, and the crab was wearing a leaf on its head.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: "It was the size of a BASKET," says (subject). "And there was no leaf." (friend) folds (friend.his/her) arms. "There's always been a leaf." The argument draws in the whole gathering. By the end, nobody can agree on the crab, the basket or the leaf, and the story has never been funnier.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (subject) opens (subject.his/her) mouth to object, then closes it. The leaf is a good detail, honestly. Next time (subject) tells the story, (subject.he/she) puts the leaf in too. Within a year everyone agrees the leaf was always there.
